decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom is a strategic option still awaiting its 2019 release, so its uncertainty is unresolved and abandoning it before market feedback would forfeit its value.
Small volume chambers serve growing small-field and SRS dosimetry needs, cost little to keep in a catalog the firm already maintains, and have shown no negative signal.
This second small volume chamber partly overlaps with Product B, but holding both options is cheap while demand for small-field dosimetry is still resolving.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is a core dosimetry item with steady demand and low carrying cost, so there is no reason to abandon it.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the firm's water phantom and scanning workflows at little marginal cost, so keeping the option open is justified.
The thimble chamber is a low-cost staple of a dosimetry portfolio and has a dedicated page with no signs of underperformance, so it stays.
